title: Run resumable global Photo purge

gates.name: Global Photo purge tests
gates.command: uv run --locked --env-file .env.local python -m pytest tests/inventory/test_hard_purge.py tests/inventory/test_photo_inventory_api.py tests/processing/test_shared_worker.py tests/promo/test_qr_continuation_api.py tests/diagnostics/test_evidence_persistence.py

evidence_required: FT-012-AC-003, FT-012-AC-004, FT-012-AC-005 and FT-012-AC-007 RED: no durable confirmed Photo snapshot, restore exclusion, purge API/UI or restartable inventory orchestration exists; GREEN: one next-linear singleton row freezes the sorted inactive-Photo UUID set, restore/restore-all exclude its non-terminal members, the existing worker waits without preemption then reports completed/total and resumes the same prefix after two crash points, and owner boundaries remove all snapshot Photo/media/face/pipeline state while retaining Promo sessions/results, core Attempts, diagnostic evidence and historical N; decisive comparison: one shared disposable PostgreSQL/MinIO/worker matrix distinguishes each AC by snapshot membership, waiting/progress observations, before/after restart prefix and complete owned-versus-retained state inventory; artifact: migration output, runtime traces, object/row manifests and focused redacted results under .tasks/TASK-110-T3-FT-012-W3/.

REQ-INV-003 project-wide authorization RED: no restore-all or hard-purge surface currently enforces the accepted administrative access and mutation guard; GREEN: active operator and developer principals can read purge state and mutate with matching CSRF, while a missing, invalid, expired or revoked session returns 401 and a photographer, unauthorized principal or missing/mismatched CSRF returns 403 without changing Photo visibility, purge-run or worker state; decisive comparison: disposable role/session/CSRF fixtures snapshot all three state owners before and after each allowed and denied request; artifact: focused redacted authorization results under .tasks/TASK-110-T3-FT-012-W3/.
purpose: Deliver the accepted project-wide restore-all and irreversible hard purge as one minimal fixed-snapshot operation on the existing worker.
success_outcome: An active operator or developer can restore every eligible inactive Photo or confirm one global purge that waits, progresses and resumes to complete owner-safe deletion, while unauthorized requests leave all state unchanged.
anti_goals: Do not add per-photo purge state, a purge jobs/targets/history table, generic retry framework, extra worker, priority or preemption.
Do not add statistics behavior, production deployment/configuration or an external cleanup service.
Do not delete, rebuild or recalculate Promo results/sessions, core Attempts, diagnostic evidence, Calibration input or issued N.

forbidden_scope: Production PostgreSQL/MinIO, operator/default Photos, live worker processes and external backups
Promo result/session, core Attempt, diagnostic evidence, Calibration and serving-control writes
Per-photo purge state, jobs/targets/history tables, new worker/service, scheduler, priority and preemption
Production deployment, ports, credentials, timers and destructive host operations
stop_conditions: The fixed snapshot and restart prefix cannot fit one singleton run row without a jobs/targets subsystem or architecture change.
Correct cleanup requires direct foreign writes, ownership-crossing cascades or deletion/recalculation of retained session/Attempt/evidence state.
Shared-worker precedence conflicts with the accepted Calibration operation or requires preemption/another worker.
Any destructive or restart probe cannot use explicit disposable state, safe rerun and complete owned cleanup.

constraints: Primary orchestration owner and expected code root are inventory at src/face_moment/inventory/; crossed public boundary is inventory -> processing and HTTP/entrypoints remain adapters.
Processing remains the only writer of ProcessingRuntimeStatus and exposes the guarded enter/leave hard_purge operations that inventory orchestration calls.
Create one next-linear inventory_hard_purge_run migration from the execution-time direct predecessor; prove only its upgrade/downgrade, schema transition and preserved prerequisite data.
Persist one sorted target UUID array and completed prefix in a singleton row; replace only a completed prior run and never append late soft deletes.
Worker ticks check confirmed/running purge before ordinary Photo claims after the active Photo/Calibration operation ends; uploads may still commit pending work.
Require an active operator or developer for every project-wide route and matching CSRF for restore-all and purge confirmation; denied requests never mutate inventory, purge-run or worker state.
Use only synthetic disposable PostgreSQL rows, private test object prefixes and deterministic backend/worker restart with safe rerun and complete cleanup.
invariants: Non-terminal snapshot members cannot be restored and the fixed target set never changes.
Progress advances only with the transaction that removes the target Photo after owner-approved object and processing cleanup.
Restart resumes the same run and completed prefix; it never restarts from a new snapshot or silently abandons a target.
Only snapshot Photo-owned data is deleted; late soft deletes, Promo/session, Attempt, diagnostics, Calibration and issued N remain unchanged.
The accepted singleton worker and direct owner boundaries remain the only runtime and coordination mechanisms.
verification_targets: A disposable migration fixture proves the singleton UUID-array/prefix constraints, execution-time linear predecessor, upgrade/downgrade/re-upgrade and preservation of existing prerequisite data.

A disposable operator/developer/photographer/session/CSRF matrix proves authorized reads and mutations, exact 401/403 denial classes and unchanged Photo, purge-run and worker state after every denial.
One fixed-snapshot scenario proves individual/global restore exclusion, late soft-delete omission, safe empty snapshot, overlapping-confirmation rejection and exact waiting/progress API/UI state.
Idle, Photo-busy and Calibration-busy worker traces prove no preemption, purge precedence after release, concurrent upload continuity and no extra worker/scheduler.

Two injected crash points plus backend/worker restart prove the same run_id, target array and prefix converge without duplicate progress; final row/object inventory proves complete owned deletion and retained Promo/session/Attempt/evidence state with missing-media skip and unchanged N.
